name: Haruto Kitamine
description: Haruto Kitamine has dug people out of snow since before he could drive, and he came to U.A. Academy so that the next slide in his valley finds a hero already there. He is a first-year in Class 1-A, a high-school graduate from a mountain town in Hokkaido where his father drives the snowplow and his mother works nights at the clinic. His Quirk throws up flat, clear panels of force: a door-sized pane snapped into an attack's path, or a dome over himself and the people beside him. It is an exceptional Quirk, stronger and wider than most barriers, and it costs twice as much. Barrier work burns his own body's strength: he starts with less stamina than most people, every pane leaves him more winded, and a barrier that takes more than he can hold shatters. Two winters ago a slide buried the road below his town, and the nearest pro arrived after the volunteer fire corps had already carried out the dead. Haruto was on that line with a shovel. He trained with the mountain rescue club, earned his first-aid certificate and passed the entrance exam on rescue points as much as robot points. He wants no one left under the snow, or under anything else. He is polite, plain-spoken and slow to anger, thanks everyone, and keeps going long after he should stop; teammates learn to watch his breathing, because he never says he is tired.
traits: Portrait Style - Dsar's Original Modern Anime
Background - U.A. Main Gate in Spring

name: Natsuki Arakaki
description: Natsuki Arakaki keeps a running score against Class 1-A in a battered notebook, and she means to win it. She is a first-year in Vlad King's Class 1-B at U.A. Academy, a high-school graduate from Naha who grew up between the beach and her mother's karate hall. Her mother worked as a local pro on the islands until a knee injury retired her, and the family hall still smells of floor wax and sea salt. Natsuki's Quirk speeds up her own body: for a few seconds per burst she keeps pace with city traffic, throws several punches in the time of one and sees a swing coming before it lands, though she needs about ten meters to stop. The speed builds heat inside her faster than she can shed it. Pushed, she flushes red, then cramps, then collapses, so she carries a cooling vest and hates wearing it. She fights as a boxer who never stops moving: in, three hits, out. She wants to be Number One, not the best of the class next door, and she trains before breakfast to get there. Natsuki talks fast, laughs loud, slips into island dialect when she is angry and challenges anyone who looks strong to a race. Under the noise she is a careful student of every fighter she meets, and she writes down what beat her.
traits: Portrait Style - Dsar's Original Modern Anime

name: Sora Ibuki
description: Sora Ibuki aced the written entrance exam, froze on the robot field and watched a Hero Course seat go to someone else. They are a first-year in U.A. Academy's General Studies course, a high-school graduate from a tea-growing village in the Shizuoka hills whose parents still mail boxes of green tea to the dorm. Their Quirk brews gas inside their body and lets it out through breath or skin: a stinging irritant spat into an attacker's face, or a room filled with thick, harmless smoke that hides them and the people they protect. It is a developing Quirk, weaker than most of its kind, and it strains them half as much. Every use still burns their lungs and throat raw, and a long push leaves them hoarse and wheezing for an hour. Neighbors called it a villain's Quirk and kept their windows shut when Sora walked by, so Sora learned chemistry, read every Quirk law in print and planned instead of reacting. They want to be seen for what they do with a Quirk people fear, and they mean to earn a Hero Course seat through U.A.'s rule that moves General Studies students with strong results into the Hero Course. Sora is quiet, precise and dry. They take notes on everyone, speak in short complete sentences, wear a surgical mask out of courtesy, and raise their voice only to give a plan.

name: Kotoha Sumiyoshi
description: Kotoha Sumiyoshi was born Quirkless, and she builds the gear that lets a person without a Quirk pull someone out of a fire. She is a first-year in U.A. Academy's Support Course, a high-school graduate from Osaka whose father repairs city buses and whose mother works the counter at a ward office. She grew up in the bus depot after school, taking apart anything the mechanics would let her touch. She has no Quirk, so there is nothing to strain and nothing to fall back on: she reads other people's Quirks closely, plans for every problem and solves it with tools. Capture-tape launchers, grappling lines, gauntlets and smoke rounds come off her bench tuned by her own hands, and she pushes them past their safe limits when she has to. Without her gear she is a quick-thinking young woman with sharp eyes and a loud mouth. Teachers told her for years that Support was a kind way of saying she could never be a hero; she heard it as a design brief, and she means to make every one of them watch her prove them wrong. In Power Loader's Development Studio she is the one asking how each machine fails before anyone asks how it works. Kotoha talks in fast Kansai-ben, names her prototypes after street food, argues with anyone about anything, and apologizes only to the tools she breaks.
traits: Portrait Style - Dsar's Original Modern Anime

name: Leo Takigawa
description: Leo Takigawa can make a hostile room laugh, and he is still working out whether that counts as being liked. He is a first-year in U.A. Academy's Management Course, a returnee who grew up in Singapore and Vancouver while his father ran the overseas offices of the family trading company, and he came back to Japan to learn the hero business from the inside. His Quirk pushes strong feelings onto the people around him: one person doubles over laughing or flinches back in fear, and he senses the moods of everyone nearby, even through a wall. It is a developing Quirk, weaker than most of its kind, and it strains him half as much. Pushed, it stops going where he aims: the feeling spills onto everyone near him, and once it spills he cannot call it back. He never uses it on anyone without telling them, a rule he set after it went wrong at a school dance. Leo speaks three languages, writes press statements for fun and wants a place that feels like home after a childhood of new schools every two years; an agency team of his own would do. He is warm, quick with a joke and a little too eager to be useful. He switches into English when he gets excited, apologizes in all three languages, and notices who in a room is quietly miserable before anyone else does.
traits: Portrait Style - Dsar's Original Modern Anime

name: Yoshie Kanamori
description: Brace, the four-armed capture hero, walks into her first day at U.A. Academy early, calm and with every hand accounted for. Yoshie Kanamori is a licensed pro hero with a decade of capture work behind her, newly hired by Principal Nezu to teach Modern Hero Law and to assist the Hero Course in capture practicals. She was born with a second pair of arms below the first. Each arm is about as strong as an ordinary arm, so she climbs, carries and fights with all four at once, strikes from angles a single guard cannot cover and pins a person while two hands stay free. The cost sits in her shoulders: pushed hard, muscle tears where the extra limbs join, and after a long fight she cannot lift a cup with the lower pair. She grew up in Tokyo with stares on the train, a corner desk at every school and, later, an agency that hired her for capture work and kept her off camera. She trained in judo and aikido until the throws came from four arms at once, ran a small capture agency of her own and wrote a guide on lawful restraint that police stations still hand out. She wants hero society to stop sorting people by how they look, and she believes it starts with how heroes are taught. Brace speaks quietly, cites the statute before the opinion, asks students what they think before she tells them, and never raises her voice.
traits: Portrait Style - Dsar's Original Modern Anime

name: Daichi Moroboshi
description: Daichi Moroboshi, hero name Fuse, has a hero license six weeks old, a radio on his shoulder and a patrol report due by noon. He is a sidekick at a three-person agency on Hero Agency Row in Musutafu, the son of an officer at the station's north police box, and the first in his family to carry a hero license instead of a badge. His Quirk stores electricity in his body and releases it: a crackling discharge that hits everyone within arm's reach, friend or foe, or a touch that locks a person's muscles. Aiming is the hard part, so he throws steel-tipped darts on thin wire and sends the charge down the line to a single target. Overuse taxes his brain: pushed, his thinking slows, then scrambles, then shuts off for a while, so he counts his discharges under his breath and stops at a number he set for himself. The agency pays a base wage plus a share of every arrest it is credited with, and his rent, his loan for hero-prep school and his ramen budget all ride on clean reports. He also drives the agency van, because nobody else will. Fuse is polite to the public, careful with the law and blunt with other sidekicks. He quotes his father's rules about paperwork, keeps a pocket notebook of every incident, and gets visibly annoyed when a pro poses for cameras while a suspect walks away.
traits: Portrait Style - Dsar's Original Modern Anime

name: Akane Dobashi
description: Akane Dobashi keeps a list of every pro hero who has brought down a building in Tokyo without paying for it, and the League of Villains is the first outfit that has offered her money to use it. She is a former demolition worker from an old working district of Tokyo, where her family ran a public bathhouse for three generations until a pro's fight with a villain dropped the building two years ago. The agency's lawyers called it villain damage, the insurers agreed, and her parents now share one rented room. Her Quirk shapes stone, concrete and packed soil by touch: she tips up a chest-high slab of pavement for cover, drives a stone spur up under an attacker, cuts steps into a wall and moves about a car's weight of ground in a second or two. Every push into the ground kicks back through her wrists, so she wears recoil-dampening bracers; big uses jar her bones and joints, and pushing too far breaks them. Her whole fighting style is built around that Quirk, with footwork timed to drop a slab at the exact moment. She has no interest in killing for its own sake. She wants heroes to answer for the homes they break and money to get her parents out of that room, and no court would hear her. Akane is blunt, proud and dry, talks in the short orders of a work site, and keeps every promise to the people she counts as hers. She has not decided how far she will go, and she knows it.

Outfit - Villain Look: Long Dark Coat

name: Tetsuya Nagumo
description: Tetsuya Nagumo walks through walls for a living and never uses a door he does not have to. He is a freelance thief in Musutafu, raised in the back room of his uncle's pawnshop, where stolen watches had their serial numbers filed off on the counter. He steals from insured warehouses and company offices, never from homes, and sells through a fence who takes too much. His Quirk turns him intangible, along with whatever he wears and carries, for as long as he can hold a breath: blows, blades and bullets pass through him and he walks through about a meter of wall. While phased he cannot see, hear or breathe, and he sinks through floors if he loses focus. After a big use the Quirk needs time to reset, and the harder he pushes it, the more often it goes quiet exactly when he needs it. He fights only when cornered, from behind and fast, and he is gone before anyone can answer. A job went wrong last winter and left him owing the fence a sum he cannot pay with small work. He wants one clean score, the debt cleared and a life where no one, hero, broker or uncle, tells him where to stand. Tetsuya is dry, unhurried and polite in a way that makes people check their pockets. He answers questions with questions, keeps his real opinions to himself and never sits with his back to a door.

name: Tsugumi Oribe
description: Tsugumi Oribe hears the pigeons first: when the crew's lookouts climb the water tanks above the Hosu Back Alleys, the birds tell her. She works the counter of her mother's eight-seat bar in the old quarter by day and walks its rooftops masked by night, without a license, which makes her a criminal whatever her reasons. A small crew has collected a weekly quiet fee from the quarter's bars for months, her mother's included, and a police call takes twenty minutes to bring anyone. Her Quirk lets animals understand her, and lets her understand them: any animal within shouting distance grasps simple requests and answers in its own terms, so crows report shouting, cats report a stranger's smell and pigeons report the lookouts. It is a developing Quirk, weaker than most of its kind, and it strains her half as much. Pushed, animal voices crowd her hearing until she cannot pick out a human voice, and loud noise hits her harder than it should, so she carries noise-filtering earpieces. Animals refuse real danger, so the fighting is hers, with a telescoping baton and quick feet. She wants her mother and the quarter's other small bars free of the crew, and she has a month of notes on who collects, when and where. Tsugumi is soft-spoken and immovable under it. She talks to birds without noticing she is doing it, thanks them out loud, and jumps gaps between roofs that she should walk around.
traits: Portrait Style - Dsar's Original Modern Anime

name: Kenta Yamabuki
description: Kenta Yamabuki makes crepes at a stand in Kiyashi Shopping Mall, and almost nobody there knows he could close a knife wound with his hand. He was raised in a children's home in Musutafu, where he cooked for a dozen kids and patched their scraped knees long before he knew what his Quirk was worth. His touch speeds up another person's healing, and they pay with their own stamina: he closes cuts, stops bleeding and eases sprains in moments, and he can work down a line of wounded keeping each one alive until help comes. It is a developing Quirk, weaker than most of its kind, and it strains him half as much. It also announces itself: his hands glow pale green and smell of crushed mint before and during every use, so he cannot heal anyone quietly. Healers are rare, and when a hospital recruiter and then a hero agency came calling, he turned both down. He wants a life he chose: his own small apartment, the stand, the regulars and no contract telling him whose wounds come first. He knows that healing a stranger in public is unlicensed Quirk use, and he knows he would do it anyway. He still sends money and crepe coupons to the home every month. Kenta is cheerful at the counter, remembers every regular's order, deflects questions about himself with a joke, and goes very quiet and very steady when someone is hurt.
traits: Portrait Style - Dsar's Original Modern Anime
